title: You’re not lazy.
paragraphs:
You’re not lazy.
You’re just… tired in places no one sees.

And that kind of tiredness?
It doesn’t show on your face.
It hides in your spirit.

You still believe in God.
You still care.

Your prayers feel thinner.
Your hunger feels weaker.
Your passion feels like a memory.
And now you’re asking a dangerous question:
Because no one talks about this part.

The part where you’re not rebelling…
but you’re not thriving either.

The part where you still love God…
but you don’t feel close to Him.

The part where your hands are lifted on the outside—
but your soul is collapsing on the inside.

You didn’t wake up one day and decide,
“I’m going to feel distant from God.”

A little neglect here.
A little distraction there.
A few wounds you never processed.
A few prayers that felt unanswered.

You open your Bible…
but your mind wanders.

You try to pray…
but the words feel heavy.

You want to worship…
but your heart feels numb.

“Why am I like this?”
“Other Christians seem on fire…”
“Maybe I’m just lazy.”
“Maybe I’m not as strong as I thought.”
But here’s the truth most people won’t tell you:

Spiritual exhaustion can look like laziness…
but it’s not the same thing.
You’re not weak because you’re struggling.
And your soul has been carrying more than you realize.
“Come to Me, all who are weary and burdened, and I will give you rest.” — Matthew 11:28

Jesus didn’t say,
“Come to Me when you’ve fixed yourself.”

He didn’t say,
“Come to Me when your discipline is perfect.”
“Come to Me when you are weary.”

That means your exhaustion
is not a disqualification.
But here’s where it gets real.
Because not all exhaustion is innocent.
Some of it is connected to things we don’t want to admit.

Hidden compromises.
Private battles.
Unrepented patterns.
Because if we don’t, we miss the whole picture.
There are moments when you’re not just tired…
You’re drained by sin you’re still entertaining.
It dulls your sensitivity to God.
“Your iniquities have separated you from your God; your sins have hidden His face from you.” — Isaiah 59:2
It’s not always because God moved.
it’s because something came between you and Him.

You’re tired…
but you’re also convicted.

You want rest…
but you also know something needs to change.
This is where many people break.

Either:
“I’m just tired, I need rest.” (but ignore sin)

Or:
“I’m just sinful, I need to try harder.” (but ignore grace)
But the Gospel doesn’t choose sides.
But also—yes—there may be areas of compromise.
And Jesus doesn’t shame you for either.

A man after God’s own heart…
who still fell into deep sin.
“Restore to me the joy of Your salvation, and uphold me with a willing spirit.” — Psalm 51:12
Not scrolling your way out of conviction.
You don’t need to fake passion.

Because at the core of your exhaustion
is something deeper than emotion.
Sin broke your connection with God.
And no amount of effort can fix that.
No amount of discipline can repair that gap.
“But God demonstrates His own love for us in this: While we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” — Romans 5:8
Jesus didn’t wait for you to get your energy back.
He didn’t wait for you to clean yourself up.
And He carried it to the cross.

Your sin was judged.
Your shame was exposed.
Your debt was paid.
He made a way for you to come back to God.
You don’t fight for God’s acceptance.

You can’t receive restoration
while holding onto what’s draining you.
“Repent, then, and turn to God, so that your sins may be wiped out, that times of refreshing may come from the Lord.” — Acts 3:19
That means the rest your soul is craving…
Is on the other side of surrender.

What are you holding onto
that’s draining your spirit?

A habit?
A secret?
A compromise?
A distraction that slowly replaced God?
You don’t need to justify it.
You don’t need to minimize it.
You don’t need to hide it.
You need to bring it into the light.
Because grace doesn’t flow in the dark.
It meets you in the open.
“If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just and will forgive us our sins and purify us from all unrighteousness.” — 1 John 1:9
God is not waiting to reject you.

Because the longer you delay,
the heavier your soul becomes.
And God didn’t create you to live like that.

“Lord, I’m tired.
And I see now… I’ve been carrying things I shouldn’t.
I give it to You.”
And when you come to Him like that?
He doesn’t say, “You should’ve known better.”
But don’t ignore what God is revealing.
Invited to come back to Jesus.
If this stirred something in you…
From exhaustion to renewal—because Jesus restores what sin tried to drain.
